title: Roll migrate back when a required render fails
lead: `--require-render` snapshots `index.json`, `log.jsonl`, `slices/`, and `render/`. `migrate` also writes `config.json` and `templates/`, and it can create a project that was not there yet.
**Not in this slice:** `done --render`, the default save-then-exit-1 policy, or the TUI.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: `_require_render` calls `store.load` before the handler, so `migrate --render --require-render` in an empty directory exits `code="state"` ("no .slicer/ found") instead of migrating. When the working directory is inside an existing project, that load snapshots the ancestor, while `migrate` writes a new `.slicer/` in the directory it was given. A render failure restores the ancestor and leaves the new tree in place, and the error envelope still says nothing was published. On `migrate --force` in the same project, index and slices roll back, and `config.json` plus templates do not: a custom row template is replaced by the defaults, and a config that omitted a status label gains it.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/cli.py` (`_require_render`, `_project_snapshot`, `_restore_project`)
- `src/slicer/migrator.py` only if the write set has to be shared
- `tests/test_cli.py` or the migrate tests

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `migrate --render --require-render` in an empty directory whose render then fails leaves no `.slicer/` behind. The exit is 2 and the code is `render`.
2. The same command with the working directory inside an existing project does not leave a new nested `.slicer/` when render fails, and it does not modify the ancestor.
3. `migrate --force --render --require-render` on a project with a custom `templates/row.md` and a config that omits a stock status label restores those files as well as the index, log, slices, and render output.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Snapshot the directory the handler will write, not an ancestor discovered before `migrate` creates `.slicer/`. Include `config.json` and `templates/`, and skip the lock. If that directory did not exist, delete what the failed command created. Do not call `store.load` early enough to reject a create-path migrate. Keep the promise on the `render` error: state and generated output are as they were before the command.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The three cases above pass. A successful `migrate --render --require-render` still writes the project and the render output. Other commands' `--require-render` rollback still passes. The suite and `slicer check` pass.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit. Do not tag or push.
